title: Project Forward - Booyah Marketing x Capital A

sentences.text: Yeah, Just a lead on where your strategy is on your acquisition journey at the moment and see if there's a fit really with what our clients looking to do.
So Booyah, I mean you're pretty sizable, aren't you?
You're working in the media buying space.
Yep.
Yeah, Booyah's about 100 person agency.
We have been in the, in the media buying space, digital media buying space for 20 years.
Focus on search, social, programmatic, pretty much anything digital, largely performance based stuff.
Do a lot of work in the finance space, travel, tourism, health and beauty.
Kind of top verticals, almost all B2C.
We do have a little bit of B2B in our kind of SEO and email kind of service offerings, but those are not a huge part of the business by revenue.
Okay.
And your, your track record on acquisitions, you've.
You've made a few already?
Yeah, Yep.
We.
I think we've done three.
Well, sort of two and a half, I guess.
First one been about five years ago, then three years ago and then about two years ago.

Looking at sort of the typically like clients in the million dollar EBITDA range and ideally clients that are doing similar things things to what we're doing already so that we can kind of just integrate teams and clients and things like that, but in a space that we already know well.
Okay, brilliant.
Yeah.
So our client is Mason Interactive.
And did you get the IM for that already?
I did, yeah.
I had a couple questions about it that are just not, not necessarily like who are these people?
But like with the, the clients like the revenue figures like so top 10 clients by revenue.
Client A is like 2.2 million.
Is that, is that the 2.2 million off of total income or is that 2.2 million off of gross profit?
I can only guess.
I think it must be of total.
Of total agency revenue.
So it's quite a large percentage.
They've got a.
Okay, yeah, yeah.
But they do actually have quite a lot of revenue under management for their clients.
I don't have the exact number in front of me, but I'm sure you'll be able to get that from ball up.
So they're mostly in entertainment and education.
I think they've got a bit of, a bit of financial stuff there as well, and tech.
Okay.
Mostly entertainment and education.
Kind of the sort of bigger niches.
Sorry, go on.
The.
Is it.
Is it mostly B2B or is it.
Is it like the, is it B2C?
Primarily education and finance and those types of things.
I guess they could fall kind of.
Either way, but I think it's.
There's a lot of B to B2C.
It's entertainment stuff is.
Is kind of their, one of their big mixes that they're involved in.
So, you know, marketing for, you know, like pop music and you know, that sort of thing.
So it's not, it's not a music agency, but more, more just sort of on the entertainment side.
Okay.
Okay, cool.
Yeah, I didn't see any examples of that in the case studies, but the education for sure.
Rowan College, they do beauty and fashion and some other stuff.
I think they've probably got more of the beauty and fashion actually up on their site as examples of stuff that they do.
Yeah.
Around the paid media stuff.
So.
Okay, is.
Is a lot of their work like creative or is it, is it more on the media side?
So I think a big portion of it is on the buy side and then they do some of the creative as.
As well.
Okay.
With the creative assignment, they'll kind of add on to the media.
I think it's, it's almost equal.
Okay, is that, is that what your mix is?
Are you doing any of the creative or are you just in the buy side?
We do some creative.
We do have a small creative department.

I would say that our creative work is not, we're not the agency you come to when you want to like have a new brand strategy, where the agency that you come to when you want to take something to market, sell it.
Yeah, I think they're the same to be honestly.
So you wouldn't, you probably wouldn't get to them first, but if you're already up and running.
Yeah, they would be able to, you know, do some of the creative and get out the door.
So.
Yeah, like our creative does like production work basically.
Yeah, that sort of thing.
Okay, so it sounds like there's probably like a fit and a good conversation you guys can have in terms of like your capital, I guess.
Is it self funded or are you looking to take on debt to do a deal?
Most of the deals we're doing are trying to self fund and we have a balance sheet to support that.
We have taken like SBA loans in the past and use those for acquisitions as well, so kind of options.
But that's why we look for kind of lower EBITDA sort of acquisition targets, acquisitions.
And the other thing is in terms of deal structure and maybe you haven't really done enough deals to know what you would offer next.
But are you looking for buy in from the founders?
Do you want them to stay in long term?
Do you have rollover equity into the holding co, or do you have anything?
We've.
We've structured things different ways and.
And tried different things often.
One of the initial questions we like to kind of get to the bottom of is, is what the founders are looking for in the transaction.
You know, I noticed that there's.
There's three founders, so there's.

I suspect that the answer is, you know, one of them wants to go, you know, sell a yacht, and one of them wants to stick around and keep things, you know, gas in the tank, and the other one is not sure.
So it is mostly Brooke.
So Brooke is in charge of the day today, and he's the majority founder and shareholder.
So there are some other founders.
Shareholders, should I say, that still involved.
Okay.
But.
But much less.
So Brook is the main man.
He's.
Yeah, he's the guy that will be in the driving seat going forward.
What does Brooke want to do with this transaction?
What's his goals?
Yeah.
So I'll give you a bit of background on this.
So we.
We actually did a transaction with Brooke last year where we sold him one of our clients businesses.
And because of that, there's been some press around us working with Mason Interactive.
And then somebody actually approached us and said, look, we'd really like to speak to Mason.
They're the kind of business we want to buy.
So I approached Brooke and he said, I'm not really interested in selling, but I'd definitely be interested having a conversation.
So actually, we've.
We've kind of coaxed him into this situation, but now he's quite happy to have these conversations.
But he is keen to be part of something bigger.
I think that's.
That's the.
The game that he's looking to play.
He's not.
He's not really in a.
In a rush at all.
Had we not approached him, he probably wouldn't have gone to market for another year or two.
So.
Um, but.
But he's.
Yeah, I mean, he's keen to be part.
Something bigger, so he's not looking to get out.
He's not looking to leave.
He wants to build.
You know, he's a creator and a builder, and he wants to do more with what he's got.
Okay, cool.
So he's looking for a structure that allows him to sort of participate in a second kind of bite.
Yeah, something like that.
Take some value off the table and.
And go for it again.
Yeah, okay.
Yeah, that's cool.
That's something that we can definitely sort of organize around.
Okay, brilliant.
So for us, it's really important to get sort of founder buy in.
Sort of first step, really, is to get you and Brooke in a room.
Obviously you give them the big picture and Brooke can tell you any questions that you've got, the technical stuff as well.
And if there is some chemistry, obviously, and you want to move forward, then that's the time we can start digging into the data room.
And, you know, if you're keen to get an offer on the table, do you have, like, again, I don't know if you've done enough deals to know whether it would just be a guess.
But in terms of like a sort of time frame, in terms of getting enough route, are you able to do them relatively quickly?
It's just obviously we're running a process on behalf of Brooke, so we have quite a bit of interest, but we would like to get offers on the table within the next three to four weeks.
Yeah, I would say we can move pretty quickly in the case where, you know, Target is, you know, lines up and checks all the boxes for us.
You know, I feel like there's some gaps in sort of what I feel like I'm able to understand about the business based on the sim, you know.
Yeah, of course, yeah.
So obviously we could just dive into those once.
Once you and Brooke have hit it off, which I'm sure you guys will.
He's definitely similar type of guy to you, so he's a really good.
He's a fun guy, actually.
He's got some good stories, so definitely enjoy.
Cool.
Yeah.
And then we can.
We can jump straight into any questions you've got.
So if you've got a list of things that you don't understand right now, then we will be.
Be happy to chip our way through them if.
If Brooke hasn't got the answers to hand either, we'll be able to get them to you straight after that call.
Okay.
All right, yeah, that sounds good.
In terms of when we could reconnect, I'm going to be sort of on the road here starting tomorrow through the following Wednesday.
So, like, late next week would be the first time that I could get that organized, if that works for you guys.
Yeah, no problem.
We've actually got a block of calls that we're doing this Friday afternoon, but we'll probably be full up by now, I should imagine.
So Thursday maybe, or Friday would be better.
I think probably either Thursday or Friday should work.
Monday morning or afternoon, definitely late afternoon.
I'm just kidding.
It's my Friday.
I used to.
I used to do a bunch of work and we.
I'd fly to London for it, and it seems like it was always like the late call that somebody wanted.
It's like, okay, cool, I guess we'll do that at 10pm then.
No, mornings are fine.
Okay, so mornings or late afternoon Thursday.
Be doable.
You know what time it's tea time at that time.
So we're all downing our tools and making cups of tea.
Yeah.
Yeah.
Okay, well, let's get that set up.
I think there's probably a good fit.
You know, what they're doing is pretty similar to you.
You're obviously ahead of them.
I would say by a little bit, but there would definitely be a good fit.
And that sounds like the right size at just over 1 million EBITDAR.
So all good.
Cool.
Okay, let's get it set up for next week.
Nice to meet you, Ryan.
Yeah, you as well.
All right, speak soon.
Cheers.
Cheers.
Bye.
Have a good day.

summary.overview: The "Project Forward - Booyah Marketing x Capital A" meeting focused on a potential acquisition discussion between Booyah, a seasoned digital media buying agency, and Mason Interactive, a firm operating in entertainment and education. Key highlights included Booyah's established record in performance-based media, its strategic focus on integrating similar-sized businesses with approximately $1M EBITDA, and its self-funding approach for past acquisitions. Mason Interactive's operations were summarized, highlighting a significant revenue contribution from a major client and its dual focus on media buying and creative services. The meeting underscored Brooke's interest in remaining involved post-acquisition while transitioning some equity. Next steps involve arranging a chemistry-building meeting between Booyah and Brooke, with both parties looking to solidify their alignment while navigating expressions of interest from multiple potential buyers facilitated by Capital A. Action items were designated to ensure readiness for the upcoming discussions.

Mason Interactive's dual focus on media buying and creative services was emphasized, alongside its significant revenue contribution from a major client. Brooke expressed a desire to remain involved after the acquisition while transitioning some equity. The next steps include scheduling a chemistry-building meeting to solidify alignment, as both parties navigate interest from multiple potential buyers facilitated by Capital A, with action items set to prepare for ongoing discussions.
